## ST303 - Linear Models

### ~~Office~~ **Student** Hours

**Student hours** are set times dedicated to all of you. Most professors call
these *"office hours"* - which I always found too formal and scary!

::: {.callout-warning title="Why student hours?"}
Students often think that *"office hours"* are times when [professors should be
left alone](https://www.chronicle.com/article/can-this-man-change-how-elite-colleges-treat-low-income-students/) - **which is the total opposite**.
I'm hoping that by calling them student hours, it might alleviate this
misunderstanding.
:::

This means that during these times I'll be waiting for you to talk to me
(either in-person or online) where you can ask whatever questions you may have.

You can [schedule a meeting with me here](https://calendly.com/cormac-monaghan-mu).
This can be either an online or in-person meeting. If you choose an online
meeting a confirmation email with a Teams link will be send to your email.

## ST303 - Linear Models {style="font-size: 90%;"}

### What we will cover

This modules aims to introduction you to the **fundamentals of linear models**
This course will cover (but is not limited to) the following:

- Statistical ideas
- Mathematical models
- Real data
- R demonstrations
- Short activities and questions
- Case studies

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## The important skill is knowing how to interpret and evaluate a linear model.
:::

## ST303 - Linear Models

### Generative AI and LLMs

AI is a thing and it's not going anywhere. However, the connection between
**AI** and **learning** is **fragile**, especially when **you are a beginner**
<br> [(see this post for more details)](https://stats.andrewheiss.com/pinky-lychee/)

> “Using ChatGPT to complete assignments is like bringing a forklift into the
> weight room; you will never improve your cognitive fitness that way.”
> [(Chiang 2024)](https://www.newyorker.com/culture/the-weekend-essay/why-ai-isnt-going-to-make-art)


::: {.fragment}
That being said, I have two rules when it comes to AI

1. **Whatever you submit must be written by you**
2. **You are responsible for checking everything that AI generates**
:::

## ST303 - Linear Models

### What does this mean in practice

```{.r filename="analysis.R"}
# I have a dataset named "penguins" and I want to calculate the number of
# different penguin types on each island. However, I can't remember the exact
# function - so I asked Gemini

# Gemini gave me two ways of doing. One using the `table()` function and another
# using the `count()` function from the `dplyr` package.
#
# I decided to use the `table()` function as I recall seeing it used in the
# lectures before

table(penguins$species, penguins$island)
```

This is a very comment heavy piece of code and it's not something you will often
see in real life. However, **for your own learning** I would recommend writing
comments like this when you decide to get help from AI <br>
**Future you will thank you when you go back to revise**.
